findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed the only employee present during today’s inspection to not have a Certified Food Protection Manager’s (CFPM) Certificate. CORRECTED- an additional employee with their CFPM arrived. A CFPM should be present at all times food is being prepared or served. Ensure a CFPM is present at all times food (that is not prepackaged) is being served.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Employees were unable to locate Employee Reporting Agreements, but did state they had signed them. Inspector will return on 10/07/25 to view Employee Reporting Agreements. Ensure they are on file and available at any time a future inspection may occur.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).[Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a biofilm accumulated around the soda nozzles. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) replaced the soda nozzles and took the ones that had been on the machine to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil residues, and to prevent contamination of ready to eat (RTE) food and drinks.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector and employees could not locate test strips that correspond with the sanitizer in the facility. The facility is using quaternary ammonia as their sanitizing solution, but have Chlorine test strips. Inspector will return on or before (if the facility obtains them before the follow up date) 10/07/25 to ensure that facility has test strips that correspond with their sanitizer solution.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the coving that seals the floor to the wall peeling from the wall underneath the electrical panel in the stock room. Reseal the coving to the wall to prevent entry of water, which could harbor mold.
2) Inspector observed a large hole cut in the drywall behind the soda boxes in the stock room. This hole exposes drywall edges and bare wood. Cover or repair this wall so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cracked and missing floor tiles in front of the self service soda station, as well as in the men’s restroom. Repair or replace tiles by the next routine inspection, so that surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Caulking around the mop sink is cracked and separated from the wall. Recaulk the mop sink.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two containers of FairLife reduced fat milk observed with manufacturer expiration dates of 11/16/2023. CORRECTED- Milk was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulk around the handwashing sink counter observed to be damaged/deteriorating. Recaulk countertop to the wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at the time of inspector’s arrival did not have proof of a food manager certification. PIC noted they have a food handler certification and are working to complete the manager certification. The store manager came back to deliver product and stayed for the remainder of inspection. Another employee with manager certification arrived for the evening shift. Ensure a certified food manager is on-site during all hours of prep/food service.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreement was not available for an employee working at the time of inspection. Employee health policy was discussed, and employee signed reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Men’s restroom hand soap dispenser was empty. Soap was provided during inspection.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Shrink wrapped packages of bottled water available for purchase were observed outside the facility on display. Store manager was advised the bottled water needs to be stored in the facility. Store manager called her supervisor during inspection so information could be shared directly with upper management. Packages of bottled water were relocated to the walk-in cooler during inspection.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreement was not available for an employee working at the time of inspection. Employee health policy was discussed, and employee signed reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Packages of raw bacon were stored above milk in the reach-in cooler section of the cooler. Manager rearranged products during inspection to allow for proper storage of raw below ready to eat foods. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 A half dozen fruit flies were observed on soda nozzles at the fountain drink machine. Staff are working to keep the service area clean. Nozzles in question were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Closely monitor the conditions at the fountain drink machine and remove nozzles for cleaning throughout the day as needed based on the current conditions concerning the presence of fruit flies.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Facility currently has a fruit fly infestation. Dozens of fruit flies were observed at and around the Froster machine and the beverage areas adjacent to the machine where coffee and fountain soda are located. Fruit flies were on the walls, surfaces of equipment, and on single service items. Flies were also observed in the restrooms, manager’s office, and sporadically in the back storage area. The Froster machine is the source of the infestation based on the conditions observed and an ongoing leak that has been an issue from the bottom of the machine. The machine has been off for 3 weeks now and certain hot food items are not being placed out for service due to concerns of cross contamination. Multiple work orders have been placed by store manager, with the most recent request for steam cleaning inside the machine being approved. The machine in question either needs to be properly cleaned and maintained to eliminate the presence of flies or should be replaced if it is beyond remediation. Call pest control company for service to assist with fly management. **See general comments for additional information.**
The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Fruit flies were observed on uncovered coffee filters located on top of the creamer dispenser at the coffee counter. Coffee filters were discarded. Store coffee filters covered in a sealed container or in original packaging.
Store manager will be discarding some items due to the presence of fruit flies on and around unpackaged single service items at the Froster machine and adjacent beverage areas.
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Employee was observed eating while working at the roller grill. Employee was advised to cease the practice of eating while working with food. Ensure employees are eating and drinking in designated areas only.
Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection can not result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands between tasks and was observed working the cash register prior to going to the drink counter and preparing coffee. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and staff were observed washing hands between tasks for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11 Sanitizer was not available for use. Manager confirmed a product called CAF Multi-Surface Cleaner and Degreaser was being used for wiping down surfaces and for sanitizing at the 3 part sink. Solution in a spray bottle did not test with any type of sanitizer test strip. Quat sanitizer was in use prior to this product but has not been available for a couple months. The practice of using the CAF product has immediately ceased. Bleach is available for use and will be used for making sanitizer solutions until quat sanitizer is obtained for use. A set of bleach test strips was provided for facility, and solutions were prepared at 100-200ppm.
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Spouts of coffee makers located above grounds basket were soiled with buildup. Ensure the spout is cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is no time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred or at least every 24 hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open packages of hotdogs in the walkin cooler were observed with date marks of 10/2 and a use by date of 10/9. Items should have been used or discarded as of 10/8 if opened on 10/2. Manager discarded hotdogs during inspection.
Also, an open package of creamer in the dispenser had a date mark of 10/5 with a use by date of 10/12. Manager was advised the use by date will be 10/11 based on opening the Saturday prior. Ensure staff know and understand date marking and proper time frame for use on required products.  
Ready to eat TCS foods shall be clearly dated after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 A chemical intended for use as a cleaner/degreaser has been used for sanitizing purposes. The manager immediately ceased using the product as a sanitizer during inspection. Product is not intended for sanitizing. Bleach will be used until quat is available for sanitization. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to the law, the FDA Food Code, and manufacturer's use directions included in labeling.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 A package of thawing hotdogs was observed under a small trickle of cold running water in the middle compartment of the 3 part sink. Proper thawing methods were discussed, and water was turned on to allow for full submersion of thawing product under water.  
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Packages of bottled water available for purchase were observed outside the facility on display. Manager was advised the bottled water needs to be stored in the facility. Cease the practice of displaying bottled water outside the facility. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the left drain board of the 3 part sink. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage area. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) cart holding hotdogs and creamer in walkin cooler (buildup);  and
B) walkin cooler shelving - two sets closest to the wall with milk, etc. (mold/buildup).
Clean the aforementioned items.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor around soda syrup boxes in back storage was soiled with splash. Clean the floor.
--Condenser fan covers, ceiling above, and attached pipes were observed with general buildup of what appeared to be dust and mold. Clean the aforementioned surfaces in the walkin cooler. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - One of the creamers was observed with date marks indicating product was placed in the dispenser on 11/22 and had a discard date of 11/29. It appeared to be a fresh bag of product, but manager was unsure as to when the product was placed in the dispenser. Manager replaced the creamer with a new bag and provided a proper date mark. Manager was also advised the use by date for the 11/22 product would have been 11/28 not 11/29. 

Packages of hotdogs and cheddarwursts in the walkin cooler had open dates of 12/29 and use by dates of 12/6. Manager was advised the use by date would be 12/5 and to change the date accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use.

Make sure everyone understands the 7 day use by time frame for date marking and that foods are getting properly dated

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 160 - Employee that had been working at the register was observed putting on gloves to handle tornados without first washing hands. When advised on handwashing, the employee stated she was preparing food for herself but would be sure to wash hands prior to glove use in the future.
Employee was then observed washing hands and shut off the faucet without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may be contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Cabinet door beneath soda fountain on the right side was observed to be damaged due to leaking liquid. Manager noted the store was due for a new drink system to be installed. Repair or replace the damaged cabinet

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following were observed to be soiled:
(R) A) walkin cooler shelves (mold/general buildup - milk section);
B) counter under roller grills and cheese/chili dispenser (dust/debris);  and
C) reach-in storage freezer (food crumbs - bottom inside/ledge under the door).

Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Package of straws was observed with liquid splash on them in the cabinet beneath the fountain soda machine. This was the same end where the cabinet door was observed damaged due to leaking liquid. Packaging was discarded, and straws that were not affected by the leak were placed out for use.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Cease the practice of storing items in the cabinet along the wall where the leak was observed until the issue is resolved.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
71130 - Mop bucket was observed to have dirty mop water inside. Manager believed it was from mopping this morning and was not yet emptied. Mop water was discarded during the inspection. 

Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.
Soiled mop water can serve as a food/water source for pests. Dispose of soiled mop water promptly via the mop sink after it is done being used.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Leak was present in the far right cabinet beneath the fountain soda machine. Manger noted a technician was out within the past few weeks because of issues with the ice maker. A leak was also present last year when the machine was new. Manager was advised to call for service to have additional repairs. The leak is affecting the cabinet and single service storage (see #15 & 25).

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(R)750.1210 & 1220 - Condenser fan covers and ceiling above the fans in the walkin cooler were soiled with dust accumulation. Clean the fan covers and the ceiling above the fans  in the walkin cooler.

Trim was missing on both sides of the wall around the new soda fountain machine, and bare wood was present. Rough, unsealed wood was also observed under/around the Home City Ice machine and the reach-in freezer. A damaged tile was also observed above the reach-in freezer.
Provide proper repairs and seal all areas with missing trim and bare wood.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Creamers in dispensers had received dates of 7/23 and discard dates of what appeared to be 8/6 & 8/16. Manager noted the creamers were just received yesterday and most likely filled this morning. Manager stated the discard date would be marked to reflect the proper time frame for use (discard by 7/30).

Open hotdogs in the walkin cooler had open dates of 7/20 & 7/21 and use by dates of 7/27 & 7/28. Manager was advised the discard dates would be one day less than what was marked on the package; the day product is opened starts day 1 of the 7 day time frame for use. Manager stated it takes about a day for products to thaw. Make sure the date the product is opened for use is accurately marked on hotdogs packages so there is no confusion. Once product is under refrigeration and opened the 7 day time frame begins. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Stem thermometer and case were observed with stuck on food debris. Manager began using a thermometer probe wipe to remove buildup. The thermometer and case would be cleaned and sanitized before the next use.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination. Use thermometer wipes on the stem thermometer between temperature checks; properly wash, rinse, and sanitize the stem and case up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Shrink wrapped packages of bottled water were observed outside the facility in the heat/sunlight. Bottled water is a food and needs to be properly stored inside the building not outside in the elements. (See General Comments)

Open packages of hotdogs were observed in the walkin cooler; packaging had holes that did not allow for sealing the bag between uses. Open the bags in a manner that allows bags to be closed/sealed between uses or provide a cleanable container with a lid to cover hotdogs once opened.

Food shall be properly stored and protected at all times.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Employee was observed wiping counters with a damp cloth that was then placed in an empty bucket. Employee stated he didn't have time to setup the sanitizer solution yet for the day. Manager setup solution (200ppm).

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (buildup);
B) counters under equipment (splash/debris);   and
C) cabinet doors below soda fountain (splash).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
Clean inside storage cabinets beneath equipment daily/as needed as well,

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Plastic clam shell containers were stored with the food surface up on top of the tornado roller grill.
Store containers covered or inverted.

Boxes of single service articles were on the floor in the back storage area.
Store single service articles up off the floor at least 6 inches.

Single service articles must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - New fountain soda machine had damp wiping cloths on both sides of the waste bin where moisture was leaking. Manager noted the machine was just installed; it was unclear as to why it was leaking or what the issue was at this time. Manager stated a work order would be placed.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 & 1220 - Condenser fan covers and ceiling above the fans in the walkin cooler were soiled with dust accumulation. Clean the fan covers and the ceiling above the fans  in the walkin cooler.

Trim was missing on both sides of the wall around the new soda fountain machine, and bare wood was present. Rough, unsealed wood was also observed under/around the Home City Ice machine and the reach-in freezer. A damaged tile was also observed above the reach-in freezer.
Provide proper repairs and seal all areas with missing trim and bare wood.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) The fresh cream dispenser does not have an internal thermometer. Provide an internal thermometer.  All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed the sani-bucket at the handsink to not have any chemical residual. Chemical was added during the inspection and solution created was 200ppm quat. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed multiple bulk boxes of cups to be stored on the floor of the back room. Store the cups at least six inches off the floor to allow for easy cleaning. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 Observed the floor and the drain under the three compartment sink to be soiled. Clean the floor and drain. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 The coving to the left of the mop sink is starting to pull away from the wall. Seal the coving to the wall.  The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 There is a new section of the wall that has been opened and pushed back for the placement of a freezer and two display racks. The opened area is framed with unsealed wood. Seal the wood.  All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed cleaners and other chemicals being stored on a shelf over the drainboard of the 3-part sink. Cease allowing chemicals to rest over clean dishes and utensils. All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed the cabinets underneath the hot holding cheeseburger display to have electrical access holes and another larger square holes. This cabinet is observed soiled in the corners. In order to protect against pests, seal the holes. UNLESS maintenance determines that these are necessary access ports for electrical etc under the cabinet island. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the cabinet mentioned in violation #15 to have accumulated materials in the corner. Discussed location of violation #s 15 and 23 with manager. Clean the island cabinets. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) Observed old, soiled mop water in the mop bucket located in the back room. Emptied during the inspection. Empty mop water immediately after use. Do not provide a water source for pests.  Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of immediately as sewage.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Overall, floors are observed in good shape. It is obvious that routine cleaning is occurring. Watch detail cleaning around the wall-to-floor areas of the 3-part sink, around the soda syrup boxes, and in the lobby around the froster machine. It appears that as mopping is being conducted the soil is being pushed into the corners around these areas.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Foods in the last two glass doors of the walk in unit next to the windows have temperature reading of between 41F and 45F.  The  750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Food was removed from the doors and placed in containers in the interior of the cooler. The temperature of foods in the interior of the cooler is 36F. It appears that the sun coming through the windows and onto the glass doors may be raising he temperature of the items in those two doors. Items on the bottom two shelves are 37F. Only the top four shelves/racks are affected.  A ticket has been put in so that the situation can be corrected.
